jobs.title: Design codex — RFC 0048 Phase C read-surface PG handlers
jobs.objective: Design PG handlers for the 8 read-surface CLI verbs that currently fall through to repo-local SQLite via CLI_ROUTES → invoke(): status, dashboard, list.runs/sessions/jobs/artifacts/workflows, run.summary, why, doctor, evidence.export, corpus.export. For each: (a) name the legacy function that owns the contract today (e.g., `src/striatum/status.py::compute_status`, `src/striatum/dashboard.py::render_dashboard`, `src/striatum/run_summary.py`, `src/striatum/cli/list.py`, `src/striatum/why.py`, `src/striatum/cli/doctor.py`, `src/striatum/evidence.py`, `src/striatum/corpus_export.py`), (b) name the new PG handler file under `src/striatum/daemon_pg/handlers/reads/<method>.py`, (c) enumerate the striatumd.* tables the handler queries (every read must be scoped by ctx.repository_id), (d) name the return-shape parity contract — the PG handler must return the same top-level JSON shape the legacy function returns today, so the CLI doesn't notice the substrate flip, (e) name the test path under `tests/daemon_pg/handlers/reads/test_<method>.py` and the parity assertion strategy (per-key diff against the legacy SQLite output on a known fixture). Track boundaries: all 8 methods are read-only, so no append-only / chain-locking concerns — design a single implement track with sub-agents per method-cluster (core: status/why/doctor/dashboard; reporting: list.*/run.summary/evidence.export/corpus.export).

jobs.title: Design claude — RFC 0048 Phase C read-surface PG handlers
Synth codex — RFC 0048 Phase C read-surface scope lock
jobs.objective: Reconcile the 2 designs (codex + claude) into one concrete plan for the 8 read-surface PG handler ports. Dogfood-060 launched with 3 designers; gemini's design lane hit a stale-lease recovery gap (see docs/dogfood/FRICTION_LOG.md dogfood-060 F1); operator dropped the gemini design slot for this restart. The remaining codex + claude designs provide adequate coverage. Lock per method: (1) legacy function path + line range that owns the contract today, (2) new PG handler file path under `src/striatum/daemon_pg/handlers/reads/<method>.py` + decorator name + signature, (3) striatumd.* tables queried (write set is empty — these are reads — but enumerate the read set for repository_id scoping verification), (4) return-shape parity contract — exact top-level JSON keys, (5) test file path + parity assertion strategy. Cross-cutting decisions: (a) repository_id scoping mechanism (WHERE repository_id = $1 discipline vs wrapper), (b) parity test rig — if claude HIGH#1 from dogfood-057 (the unused parity rig in `tests/daemon_pg/handlers/recovery_evidence/conftest.py`) is still unwired in main, decide whether to wire it now or write a simpler shape-only smoke test (justify), (c) single implement track (NO dual-track — all 8 methods are read-only and similar structure, splitting tracks creates artificial boundaries that caused the 058 cycle exhaustion). Pick one path; do not enumerate alternatives.

jobs.title: Review design claude ergonomics_dx
jobs.objective: Review synthesis. Mandatory checks: (1) all 8 read methods enumerated with legacy-function citation + new handler path + test path — bounce on any missing, (2) return-shape parity contract specified per method (not 'similar to' — exact key list), (3) repository_id scoping mechanism specified, (4) single implement track confirmed (NO dual-track), (5) parity test strategy concrete (function name, fixture path, per-key diff helper or shape-only smoke). Ergonomics_dx posture: handler error messages cite operator-actionable next commands; failure modes (repo_not_registered, no rows, malformed params) return RPC errors not silent empty results.

jobs.title: Implement RFC 0048 Phase C read-surface PG handlers (codex, single track)
jobs.objective: Port the 8 read-surface methods to PG handlers under `src/striatum/daemon_pg/handlers/reads/`: status, dashboard, list.runs, list.sessions, list.jobs, list.artifacts, list.workflows, run.summary, why, doctor, evidence.export, corpus.export. (Adjust the final list to whatever the synthesis locks — if synthesis decided some methods stay on legacy, document that in HANDOFF.) For each handler: exact module path locked by synthesis, `@register_pg_handler("<method>", read_only=True)` decorator, `def handle(ctx, params) -> dict`, queries striatumd.* tables filtered by `ctx.repository_id`, returns the same top-level JSON shape as the legacy function. Wire registration via `src/striatum/daemon_pg/handlers/__init__.py` adding `from . import reads`. Tests under `tests/daemon_pg/handlers/reads/test_<method>.py` assert: (a) handler returns the locked shape on the standard fixture, (b) returns empty/None where the legacy function does, (c) errors RPC-style on bad params (not Python exceptions). Sub-agents per cluster: core-reads (status/why/doctor/dashboard); reporting-reads (list.*); summary-reads (run.summary/evidence.export/corpus.export).

jobs.title: Build review codex threat_model
jobs.objective: Threat-model review: every read handler scopes by repository_id (a handler called against repo A returns no rows for repo B); read handlers never write — SQL is `SELECT` only, no `INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE`/`UPSERT`; capability-token check enforced (the test framework should monkeypatch authorize to deny and assert handler short-circuits); SQL is parameterized — no string interpolation that could allow SQL injection via run_id / session_id / job_id; handlers do not leak data across repositories on union queries.

jobs.title: Build review claude ergonomics_dx
jobs.objective: Operator UX review: `striatum status --json` on a migrated repo returns the same shape as the legacy SQLite path (or document the diff); `striatum dashboard --once` renders post-migration; `striatum list runs --json` returns the same row order + columns; error messages on `repo_not_registered` cite the remediation command; tests print readable diffs on parity failures (not raw dict comparisons); the V1.51 `STRIATUM_DAEMON_REQUIRED=0 STRIATUM_TEST_HARNESS=1` escape becomes purely optional for migrated repos.

jobs.title: Build review gemini adversarial
jobs.objective: Adversarial: a read handler that returns rows from the wrong repository (forgot to filter by repository_id); a handler that silently drops rows when the SQL fails (caught exception); a status handler that returns stale data because it queries a view that lags writes; a list.* handler that paginates inconsistently (different sort order between calls); a parity test that passes because BOTH the PG handler and the legacy SQLite path return empty for the wrong reason; a handler that bypasses RFC 0030 capability auth because the read methods are 'just queries'; an evidence.export handler that leaks redacted prose into the export.
